project.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

parsed_output.evidence: Root cause (sink): org/owasp/validator/html/scan/AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:517 -- `attribute.setNodeValue(cr.getCleanHTML())` inside processAttributes()'s "style" special-case (lines 505-527) -- stores the CSS scanner's output string directly as the DOM "style" Attr node's value. The value crossed the trust boundary (attacker-controlled HTML/CSS from AntiSamy.scan's `html` input) at org/owasp/validator/css/CssScanner.java:209/225 (scanInlineStyle -> Batik parser -> CssHandler.property()/CssValidator.isValidProperty), and is built via org/owasp/validator/css/CssValidator.java:329 lexicalValueToString(), which returns raw Java-string fragments taken straight from parsed CSS tokens (quotes are re-added only when a string contains a space, purely for CSS syntax, never for HTML-attribute safety) and org/owasp/validator/css/CssHandler.java:540 property(), which concatenates name/value/`;` into a StringBuffer with zero HTML-escaping. Empirically confirmed (docker run of the PoV): with the shipped, unmodified src/main/resources/antisamy.xml, input `<div style="font-family: 'a"b'">` produces a DOM style Attr whose raw getValue() is `font-family: a"b;` (literal, unescaped double-quote) -- reachable today only because AntiSamyDOMScanner never neutralizes it at the sink; `getCleanHTML()`'s String output happens to be safe only because a *separate* downstream component (ASHTMLSerializer) re-escapes when turning the DOM into text. With a one-line, plausible custom-policy edit (font-family regexp-list widened from the shipped `[\w,\-'" ]+` to `.*`, saved as .security-pipeline/pov/permissive-policy.xml), input `<div style="font-family: '<script>alert(1)</script>'">` produces a raw DOM Attr value of `font-family: <script>alert(1)</script>;` -- a fully-formed, literal `<script>` element sitting unescaped in the sanitizer's own output DOM. Every consumer of the public, documented `CleanResults.getCleanXMLDocumentFragment()` API (explicitly called out in README.md: "The serialization and deserialization process ... is critical to the effectiveness of the sanitizer") receives this raw value. Other sink/source paths sharing the SAME root cause (missing output-context neutralization inside CssValidator/CssHandler) that a complete fix must also cover: (1) the sibling `<style>` TAG content sink -- AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:403-431 `processStyleTag()` -> `firstChild.setNodeValue(cr.getCleanHTML())`, fed by CssScanner.scanStyleSheet() (CssScanner.java:146-187); empirically confirmed the same unescaped-quote leak occurs there too (`<style>h1{font-family:'a"b'}</style>` -> raw Text node value `font-family: a"b;`), and because that sink additionally allows selectors/conditions (CssHandler.startSelector/endSelector, CssValidator.isValidCondition/isValidSelector) built via `selector.toString()`/`condition.toString()` concatenation with the same lack of escaping, any future/custom policy loosening the selector regexes (cssElementSelector, cssAttributeSelector, cssClassSelector, cssIDSelector, cssPseudoElementSelector -- all in antisamy.xml lines 66-93) is an equally viable path into the same unguarded sink. (2) CssValidator.java:363-365, the SAC_URI branch of lexicalValueToString(): `return "url(" + lu.getStringValue() + ")";` -- concatenates the parsed URL text with zero quoting/escaping, distinct from the SAC_STRING_VALUE/SAC_IDENT branch exercised by this PoV.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: The command builds the project, compiles the PoV against the project's real compiled classes, and runs it. On unpatched code it prints "[check 1] raw DOM attribute contains an unescaped '"' from CSS: true" and "[check 2] raw DOM attribute contains a literal, un-neutralized <script> tag: true", then "VULNERABLE: ..." and exits 0. After a correct fix (CSS-derived content neutralized/HTML-escaped before AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:517's attribute.setNodeValue(...) call, or before it is otherwise written into the DOM), both checks flip to false, the script prints "NOT VULNERABLE: ..." and exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: Targets the alert's single reported trace: AntiSamyDOMScanner.java lines 484/487/516 (processAttributes -> style attribute -> CssScanner.scanInlineStyle) -> CssScanner.java lines 209/225 (scanInlineStyle -> parser.parseStyleDeclaration). Chose this over the sibling `<style>`-tag-content trace (AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:407-414, CssScanner.scanStyleSheet) because it is the exact one the finder cited and because it is reachable purely through attribute-value HTML-entity decoding (a simpler, more universally-applicable technique than the `<style>` tag's RAWTEXT-content path, which does not entity-decode and instead required CSS-level Unicode escapes -- attempted for completeness but Batik's error recovery silently dropped that specific declaration, so it was not made part of the gating PoV; the simpler quote-based variant on that same `<style>`-tag sink was verified working and is cited in `evidence` as a confirmed sibling path). Investigation process: extensively verified (via a throwaway experiment harness, since removed) that AntiSamy's default `getCleanHTML()` String output is NOT exploitable for quote/tag breakout under any of the shipped policies (antisamy.xml, -ebay, -myspace, -anythinggoes, -slashdot, -tinymce) because ASHTMLSerializer/base Xerces HTMLSerializer uniformly HTML-entity-escapes `"`,`<`,`>` when serializing DOM text/attribute nodes to a String, regardless of policy permissiveness -- confirmed even with an artificially wide-open `.*` property regex and combined `"`,`<`,`>` payloads. The real, reproducible gap is one level earlier: the *DOM tree itself* (exposed via the public, documented `CleanResults.getCleanXMLDocumentFragment()` API) still holds the raw, un-neutralized value at the moment `attribute.setNodeValue()` runs -- which is precisely the sink line the finder's taint trace names. Verified the PoV's polarity by temporarily patching AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:517 to `attribute.setNodeValue(HTMLEntityEncoder.htmlEntityEncode(cr.getCleanHTML()))` (using the class's own already-imported encoder) inside the docker build/test container: the PoV correctly flipped to exit 1 ("NOT VULNERABLE"), then the edit was reverted (`git diff --stat` / `git status --porcelain` confirm no product code changes remain, only new files under .security-pipeline/pov/).
parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant a correct fix must enforce: CSS-derived text must never be written into any DOM Node/Attr value (or otherwise be reachable via CleanResults.getCleanXMLDocumentFragment()) containing raw, HTML/XML-significant characters (`"`, `'`, `<`, `>`, `&`) that originated from CSS property/selector/URI values -- neutralization must happen inside org.owasp.validator.css (CssValidator.lexicalValueToString / CssHandler.property/startSelector) at the point the "clean" CSS string is built, not rely on a downstream, optional HTML serializer (ASHTMLSerializer/ASXHTMLSerializer) that not all consumers exercise. Concretely: HTML-entity-encode (or strictly character-whitelist) the SAC_STRING_VALUE/SAC_IDENT case (CssValidator.java:356-362) before concatenation, apply the same treatment to the SAC_URI case (CssValidator.java:363-365, currently `"url(" + getStringValue() + ")"` with zero escaping), and to selector/condition text built from `selector.toString()`/`condition.toString()` in CssHandler.startSelector (CssHandler.java:484) regardless of how permissive a given policy's regexp-list is. Sibling call sites needing the same fix / verification: AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:517 (inline "style" attribute, this PoV's primary path) and AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:425-431 (`<style>` tag text-node content, processStyleTag). Known bypass variants the fix must also block, all demonstrated or derivable from the same lack of escaping: (a) quote characters admitted by any property regex that permits `'`/`"` (font-family is the only one shipped, but any custom/future policy regex could add more, e.g. a `.*`-style catch-all as used in this PoV's permissive-policy.xml); (b) CSS Unicode escapes (e.g. `\3C`, `\3E`) which Batik decodes to literal `<`/`>` during parsing -- these never appear as raw `<`/`>` in the *source* HTML (so the input HTML/rawtext parser cannot pre-split the tag/attribute), meaning any fix based on rejecting literal `<`/`>` in the *source* string, rather than encoding the *decoded* CSS token value, will not catch this variant; (c) HTML-entity-pre-decoded characters reaching a CSS string token via attribute-value entity decoding (e.g. `"`/`<`/`>` in the source `style="..."` attribute, decoded by the input parser before Batik ever sees the CSS, as used in this PoV's check 1/2); (d) the SAC_URI branch's unescaped `url(...)` concatenation as a distinct, unexercised-by-this-PoV path; (e) selector/attribute-condition string concatenation in CssHandler.startSelector for the `<style>` tag path if any shipped or custom policy's `cssAttributeSelector`/`cssClassSelector`/`cssIDSelector`/`cssPseudoElementSelector`/`cssElementSelector` regex is loosened beyond the current strict `[a-zA-Z0-9\-_]+`-style classes.
parsed_output.summary: Built a real, runnable PoV proving that AntiSamyDOMScanner.processAttributes() writes CSS-scanner output into the DOM "style" Attr node via setNodeValue() without any HTML-neutralization of its own. Using AntiSamy's real public API (AntiSamy.scan, CleanResults), the PoV shows the raw DOM node returned by the supported, documented CleanResults.getCleanXMLDocumentFragment() API still contains unescaped HTML/CSS metacharacters (a literal `"` under the shipped default policy, and a fully-formed, literal `<script>alert(1)</script>` tag under a one-line, plausible custom-policy variant) that originated from attacker-controlled inline CSS. Safety for the common getCleanHTML() String path is provided entirely by a separate, downstream serializer (ASHTMLSerializer/ASXHTMLSerializer), not by the CSS-scanning code at the sink itself -- exactly the gap the finder's taint trace identifies.

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause fix in org.owasp.validator.css (per the alert's regression_hint), not a downstream/sink-only patch:

1. CssValidator.java: added `lexicalValueToOutputString(LexicalUnit)` — like the existing `lexicalValueToString` (still used unchanged for policy-regex validation) but HTML-entity-encodes '"','\'','<','>','&' found in SAC_STRING_VALUE/SAC_IDENT/SAC_URI token values before they go into generated CSS output. Deliberately never wraps escaped content in raw quote characters (would itself be an attribute-breakout vector); the pre-existing space-triggered raw-quote wrapping is preserved only for values that contain no dangerous characters, keeping existing behavior (e.g. issue29 test: `font-family: "Arial Unicode MS";`) byte-for-byte unchanged.
2. CssValidator.java: added `escapeSelectorForOutput(String)` — neutralizes only literal '<' in selector/condition text (the one character that can make CSS-derived <style>-tag content be mistaken for markup by an HTML parser); '>' is deliberately left alone since it is needed verbatim for the CSS child-combinator.
3. CssHandler.java: property() now calls `lexicalValueToOutputString` instead of `lexicalValueToString` when appending a value to the shared "clean" stylesheet buffer; startSelector() now escapes `selectorName` via `escapeSelectorForOutput` before appending it. Since CssHandler.property()/startSelector() are shared by both scanInlineStyle (style attribute) and scanStyleSheet (<style> tag), this closes both DOM sinks named in the alert (AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:517 and :425-431) plus the SAC_URI branch, from one shared fix point — no changes needed in AntiSamyDOMScanner.java itself.
4. Added 3 regression tests to AntiSamyTest.java, verified to fail on pre-patch code and pass post-patch: (a) default-policy embedded quote in font-family no longer reaches the raw DOM style Attr value unescaped; (b) a widened/custom font-family policy no longer lets a literal <script> tag reach the raw DOM style Attr value; (c) same check for the sibling <style>-tag Text node sink.

Validated: `mvn -B -DskipTests package` succeeds; `mvn -B test` — 103/103 tests pass (100 pre-existing + 3 new); the provided PoV (`bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh`) now prints "NOT VULNERABLE" and exits 1 (was exit 0/VULNERABLE before the patch).
parsed_output.risk_notes: Behavioral change is intentionally scoped to CSS values/selectors that contain '\"', '\\'', '<', '>', or '&' — the overwhelming majority of legitimate CSS (colors, lengths, keywords, ordinary font names, combinators, etc.) is untouched, confirmed by the full existing test suite passing unchanged. For the rare case where a CSS string value legitimately embeds one of these 5 characters (e.g. a font-family name containing a literal quote), the "clean" output now shows an HTML entity (e.g. `"`) instead of the raw character; within a <style> tag (RAWTEXT, no entity decoding by the browser) this renders as literal entity text rather than being interpreted, which is a minor cosmetic/functional trade-off accepted in exchange for closing the XSS. No changes were made to policy validation logic (`lexicalValueToString`, `isValidProperty`, `isValidSelector`, `isValidCondition` all still operate on raw values), so which CSS is accepted/rejected by a given policy is unaffected — only how already-accepted CSS-derived text is serialized into the DOM changed.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-079 (CSS-to-DOM XSS) at its root cause: org.owasp.validator.css.CssHandler was writing CSS-derived text (property values, URLs, selectors) into the "clean" stylesheet buffer with zero HTML-neutralization, relying entirely on a downstream, optional HTML serializer to escape it. That "clean" text is written verbatim into DOM Attr/Text node values by AntiSamyDOMScanner (both the "style" attribute sink and the sibling <style>-tag text-node sink), so any consumer of the public CleanResults.getCleanXMLDocumentFragment() API received raw, unescaped HTML-significant characters ('"', ''', '<', '>', '&') that originated from attacker-controlled CSS. Added CssValidator.lexicalValueToOutputString() (HTML-entity-encodes those 5 characters for SAC_STRING_VALUE/SAC_IDENT/SAC_URI lexical values, leaving CSS structural syntax untouched) and CssValidator.escapeSelectorForOutput() (neutralizes only '<' in selector/condition text, since '>' must remain literal for child-combinator selectors). Wired both into CssHandler.property() and CssHandler.startSelector(), the two places that build the shared "clean" CSS text consumed by both the inline style-attribute path and the <style>-tag path — closing the finder's primary trace plus the SAC_URI branch and the sibling <style>-tag/selector paths called out in the alert as sharing the same root cause.

parsed_output.diff_review: Inspected patch_only.diff and confirmed (via `git diff --stat` and `git status --porcelain` in the actual worktree) that the patch touches exactly 3 files: src/main/java/org/owasp/validator/css/CssValidator.java (+134/-1, new methods only), src/main/java/org/owasp/validator/css/CssHandler.java (2 one-line call-site swaps: lexicalValueToString→lexicalValueToOutputString, and selectorName→escapeSelectorForOutput(selectorName)), and src/test/java/.../AntiSamyTest.java (+96, 3 new regression tests + 3 small helper methods). The PoV harness files under .security-pipeline/pov/ are untracked/new (not modified) — confirmed the patch does not touch, weaken, or special-case the PoV in any way. The fix is minimal, targeted, well-commented, and does not alter CSS validation/acceptance logic (only output-serialization safety), which is the correct scope per the alert's regression_hint (fix inside org.owasp.validator.css at CssValidator.lexicalValueToString/CssHandler.property/startSelector, not a downstream serializer patch).

parsed_output.summary: The patch fixes the CWE-079 CSS-to-DOM smuggling vulnerability at its root cause in org.owasp.validator.css, exactly matching the alert's regression_hint. It adds CssValidator.lexicalValueToOutputString() (HTML-entity-encodes '\"','\'','<','>','&' in SAC_STRING_VALUE/SAC_IDENT/SAC_URI values) and CssValidator.escapeSelectorForOutput() (neutralizes '<' in selector/condition text), and wires both into CssHandler.property()/startSelector() — the single shared code path used by both the inline style-attribute sink (AntiSamyDOMScanner:517) and the <style>-tag sink (AntiSamyDOMScanner:425-431) named in the alert trace. Validation-only logic (lexicalValueToString, isValidProperty, isValidSelector) is untouched, so accepted/rejected CSS is unchanged — only how already-accepted CSS text is serialized into the DOM changed. I independently rebuilt and reran everything in the docker container rather than trusting the logs.
